rationale: Use four isolated logical PostgreSQL databases with restricted owner credentials in one local cluster. Event Management atomically freezes and returns an idempotent admission-capacity snapshot before Registration initializes its ledger. A failed local initialization retries the same remote snapshot. The user approved immutable capacity after admission activation instead of a distributed live-update protocol. This avoids stale capacity reductions causing overbooking without cross-database transactions.
invariants: No runtime service reads or changes another service's database.
Admission cannot begin without the frozen activity capacity and stable snapshot/version.
Capacity changes after activation are explicitly rejected, even when occupancy returns to zero.
Conflicting snapshots cannot overwrite an existing Registration ledger.
Missing activity validation or availability dependencies never produce permissive admission or fabricated free counts.
Remote freeze survives local failure and retries return the same snapshot.
